leads.name: Alte Eibe Hasenmatt
leads.status: unresolved, second source needed. monumentaltrees.com (id 45941, checked via a 2021-05-18 Wayback snapshot since the live page is Cloudflare-gated) is the only source found this pass: European Yew (Taxus baccata) on the Hasenmatt massif in Selzach commune (Solothurn canton, north side of the mountain), multi-stem, girth ~6m, height ~25m, dendrochronologically estimated planted circa 1225+/-100 (so ~796+/-100 years old) by named surveyor Roland Zoss, 15 Jun 2020. No precise coordinates could be recovered (the archived page's map data did not capture). Could be the SAME physical tree as the verified 'Old Yew in Cremines' (cre_001, Bernese Jura, Malsenberg/Maljon forest, south side of the same Hasenmatt massif, ~4-5km away) reported under a different municipal label and a different, more legendary age claim (1500 years vs this dendro estimate of ~800), or a genuinely distinct second ancient yew on the opposite slope. Two searches for a Solothurn cantonal Naturdenkmal register or a second independent write-up specific to Selzach found nothing (canton Solothurn's Wikipedia protected-areas list names 'Naturschutzgebiet Hasenmatt' as dry-meadow habitat only, no tree; opendata.swiss's 'Geschuetzte Einzelbaeume' dataset page 403'd). Needs either a second source or a same-tree confirmation before it can ship.

leads.name: Erlebnisbaum (Rotkreuz ZG)
leads.reason: German Wikipedia (Rotkreuz ZG) confirms this is not primarily a remarkable tree but a wooden viewing tower built in 2000 around an oak in the Sijentalwald, and the tower 'no longer stands' ('Momentan steht der Erlebnisbaum nicht mehr. Er wurde abgerissen, da das Holz morsch war'), demolished for rot, with only a vague plan to rebuild someday. The oak itself is described as about 150 years old and 30m tall, which is not exceptional (many published trees are far older) and carries no other documented distinguishing feature; its fame was entirely the tower's information panels and viewing platform, which is gone. Fails the destination test on the tree's own merits and the photographed structure no longer exists to visit. Left blocked rather than researched further; a future pass could recheck if the rebuild happens.

leads.name: Grand châtaignier d'Antagnes
leads.reason: Dead. Radio Chablais (radiochablais.ch, 2022-11-14) reports this tree, 'le chataignier des Plumasses' between Glutieres and Antagnes in Ollon (Vaud), roughly 300-500 years old per different figures, ~20m tall and ~10m in circumference, registered in 'Les Beaux Arbres du canton de Vaud', collapsed under its own weight overnight 2022-11-10/11 due to root failure. A follow-up Radio Chablais piece ('le chataignier des Plumasses renait pour perpetuer un heritage seculaire') confirms a young sapling grown from the same tree was replanted a few metres from the fallen trunk, but per hard rule the ORIGINAL tree is dead and never ships as a collectible entry; a newly planted sapling with no age of its own is not a substitute. Never re-research from zero; if the replanting matures and becomes locally notable in its own right, a future pass can look again.

leads.name: Noyer de Vilmorin de Meinier
leads.status: unresolved, access needs confirming before this can ship. Otherwise strongly verified and worth a future look: species Juglans x intermedia (a natural hybrid of common walnut and North American black walnut), 'the oldest hybrid walnut in Switzerland and the largest walnut in Switzerland' per SWI swissinfo.ch quoting Geneva canton's own urban-tree chief, planted 1863 (documented planting date, so ~163 years old as of 2026), height ~25-35m (sources vary), trunk circumference over 6m (6.4m per patrimoine-vert-geneve.ch), crown circumference 113m. Celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2013 with a canton-installed commemorative plaque, and the canton has since installed a wooden brace, cables and straps to preserve it. Two independent sources easily clear the species/age bar (swissinfo.ch and the Meinier commune's own page). The blocker is hard rule 10: both sources state it stands 'sur une parcelle privee derriere l'eglise St Paul de Meinier' (on a private plot behind the church), and neither states a public path or road passes close enough to see it, only the vaguer 'rejouit les promeneurs' (delights walkers), which is not the same as a source affirmatively saying it is visible from public ground. Needs either an OSM/aerial check for a public path or lane skirting the church that puts the tree in view, or a direct statement of public visibility, before this clears hard rule 10 as a view-only entry. Would be a strong Geneva day-trip addition (Meinier is a village a few km from Geneva) if access clears.

leads.name: Old Yew in Crémines
leads.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-05, delivered as cre_001 (data/research/_famous-switzerland-verified.json), container: new place: Cremines. Verified alive (commune's own page cites TV coverage as recent as July 2023), species European Yew (Taxus baccata), age ~1500 years per commune page and baumkunde.de register, girth 425cm, coordinates confirmed from baumkunde.de (E7 28.2884' / N47 16.3625'). Genuine destination-tier tree: widely cited candidate for oldest tree in Switzerland.
